payload.summary: Reject the first two amendments because the cited defects are not present in the current implementation path; accept the snapshot deserialization alias and overview estimate-label amendments because they fix real compatibility and user-facing correctness gaps.

votes.rationale: The claimed test failure is not reproducible in the current tree. `expected_gh_d` already uses the same full molar-mass literals as the production calculation rather than the rounded shortcut factors described in the amendment, and `cargo test -p tank_core canonical_helpers_use_net_water_volume -- --exact` passes. Widening the tolerance would weaken a valid regression check, and importing production constants into the test would reduce test independence without fixing an actual bug.

There is no real silent-propagation path here for legacy save files. `SaveFile::from_json` parses through `serde_json::from_str`, standard JSON does not admit `NaN` or infinity, and `serde_json::Value`/`Number` does not preserve non-finite numbers for this migration step. In this code path, `as_f64()` is already the effective type gate, so an additional `is_finite()` check would be redundant rather than closing an actual validation hole.

This is a real compatibility defect. The TUI deserializes `/snapshot`, `/time/step`, and `/load` responses directly into `TankSnapshot`, and `TankSnapshot` now requires the renamed chemistry fields. A newer client receiving payloads from an older server that only emits the legacy names will fail deserialization unless aliases or an equivalent compatibility layer are added.

The overview screen is still presenting estimated 7-ion TDS/conductivity values with labels that read like direct measurements. Even with the nearby scope text, the primary label line should reflect that these are estimates, especially since the chemistry screen already does. Renaming the overview labels improves user-facing correctness and keeps the UI semantics consistent with the underlying fields.
